product.name: Hold
product.tagline: One circle. Tap for a kick, hold for a session.
product.dek: Hold is a companion for the third trimester: tap the circle to log a movement, hold it to start a real session, and watch your baby's own pattern build in minutes, not tallies. There's a plain-language report ready whenever you have an appointment, one alert if a quiet stretch runs long, and Hold can still time contractions against 5-1-1 once labour starts. It runs on your phone, and it works with the screen off just as well as on.
product.note: Below is what a pregnant parent actually meets in the 2.3.0 rebuild — the circle, the pattern it builds, the one alert, and everything else Hold does that isn't about counting.

parts.kicker: Every day, from the third trimester
parts.title: One circle: tap for a kick, hold for a session
parts.dek: No form, no menu. Feel something, tap the circle and get on with your day — or hold it to start a proper session. The two hint pills underneath stay on screen permanently, because the gesture is the one thing this design asks you to learn.

features.title: Tap for one kick
features.summary: The circle on Home logs one movement the instant you tap it — nothing is debounced, two felt movements are two taps. A quiet confirmation offers to add what you were doing, but Hold never asks first.

features.title: Hold for a session
features.summary: Press and hold and the ring fills, the circle swells, and a full counting screen opens — the rhythm of your taps drawn live underneath, and the whole screen is the tap target, so you can count in the dark without aiming.

features.title: Your own words for context
features.summary: Tap a verb — Ate, Drank, Lay down, Did, Listened, Read, Watched — then type your own noun once. Hold remembers it as a chip from then on. The same sheet appears from Home's context row and again when a session ends.

parts.title: A pattern only your baby could have
parts.dek: Hold will not name a usual time of day from a handful of taps — that would teach you the wrong normal. It waits for real evidence, and shows its working the whole way there.

features.title: Nothing to say yet
features.summary: Open the Patterns tab before logging anything and the card is already there, already carrying its own caveat — “Still learning the pattern” — and states plainly what it's waiting for: at least 20 movements across at least 3 days.

features.title: Real data, not a rhythm yet
features.summary: A couple of days in, the bars have height and the counts are real — but Hold still won't name a busiest time. Two days isn't a rhythm, and naming one here would be a guess dressed up as a fact.

features.title: The pattern speaks for the first time
features.summary: The moment Hold crosses its own threshold, the card changes from “still learning” to a claim — a busiest stretch of the day, phrased as what you logged, never as a cause.

features.title: Minutes of movement, against your own usual
features.summary: Two weeks of logging later, Patterns draws a bar of minutes for every day against a marker at your own 21-day average, plus a card that says what tends to come before a session — always with the reminder that these are counts of what you tapped, not causes.

features.title: A card built to share
features.summary: Screenshot the card, or tap Share — it exports as an image carrying the week and the caveat with it, so a partner or midwife gets the whole picture in one message.

features.title: Notes live inside Patterns now
features.summary: There's no separate Notes tab any more — a note is always about a session, a day or the pregnancy, so it lives beside the thing it describes. Filter by All, Sessions, Days or Overall, search by a food you tagged, and pin the ones worth keeping at the top.

features.title: Every movement you've logged
features.summary: The full list underneath the pattern, for anyone who wants to check the raw log rather than the summary of it.
features.entry: Patterns → Every movement you have logged

parts.title: A one-page report, in plain language
parts.dek: No charts to interpret: typical day, most active, quietest, days below your usual, and any note you flagged — worded the way you'd say it out loud.

features.title: The week report
features.summary: One tap builds a plain-language page from this pregnancy's own numbers, ready to share, print, or show on screen at the appointment.

parts.title: Opt-in, against your own baseline, never reassurance
parts.dek: If a quiet stretch runs much longer than yours usually does, Hold can say so once, with the number to ring. It's off unless you turn it on, it's measured against your own pattern rather than a fixed threshold, and it never says everything is fine.

features.title: Quieter than your usual
features.summary: States what was observed and why a stretch this long is worth a call, not a wait — and it stays on screen until you call or say you've felt movement since. It never disappears on its own.
features.entry: The one alert, when it fires

parts.title: Calm, with your own audio
parts.dek: Breathe with the circle, or bring in a voice memo, a playlist, or a recording of a heartbeat from your own phone — 5, 10, 20 minutes or open-ended. Nothing is uploaded; Hold only remembers where the file is.

features.title: Calm
features.summary: Box breathing with a circle to follow, your own audio underneath it, and one steadying line that doesn't reassure about the baby — only about the person holding the phone.

parts.title: The call comes first
parts.dek: No chart, no count, no reassurance. The phone call is the only thing on this screen that outranks everything else, because delay is the harm reduced-movement guidance warns about.

features.title: Trust that feeling
features.summary: One tap to the saved triage number, self-help notes while you wait, and a gentle note if this is the second time this week — phrased as help with the call, never as a reason to hesitate.

parts.title: Contraction timing, and 5-1-1
parts.dek: Hold can still time contractions and check them against the standard 5-1-1 guide — about five minutes apart, about a minute long, kept up for about an hour — in a screen that stays strictly dark regardless of your phone's own theme, because this one gets read at 3am.

features.title: 5-1-1 met — time to call
features.summary: An hour of contractions about five minutes apart and about a minute long satisfies the rule: all three checks tick, and one tap dials your saved triage number.

parts.title: Profile, care team, and every setting
parts.dek: Personalise how the session screen looks, choose your default tap, manage your own words, care-team numbers with tap-to-call, dark theme, and the plain-text way to end a pregnancy record.

features.title: The You tab
features.summary: Every setting lives here now, in rows rather than a flat list — most show the current choice and open a screen to change it. Ending a pregnancy record deletes everything Hold has recorded immediately and stops the app asking anything else.

parts.title: The whole third trimester, in one clip
parts.dek: An almost-empty log at week 27, the pattern refusing to speak and then speaking, the transition at term, and labour with 5-1-1 firing.

features.title: The full journey
features.summary: Week 27 through to labour: taps accumulating, the two evidence gates being crossed, the transition at term, and a contraction pattern that meets 5-1-1.

privacyParagraphs: No account needed — Hold works fully without one. If you choose to sign in with a TinyKite account, only your email identifies you to us; your pregnancy data (movements, contractions, notes) stays on your phone and is never uploaded.
Every tap, every counting session, every contraction is stored in a database on your device, not on our servers. There's no cloud sync, no ads, and no analytics reading over your shoulder.

The plain-language report and the full clinical report are both built on your phone and only leave it when you choose to share or print them — through your phone's own share sheet, the same way you'd share a photo.
Ending a pregnancy record in the You tab deletes everything Hold has recorded from your phone immediately, and the app stops asking you anything else.
trust.medicalHeading: Hold is not a medical device
medicalParagraphs: Hold never diagnoses. It records what you tell it and compares it against published guidance and your own history — nothing more.

There is no set number of movements that counts as normal. What matters is your baby's own pattern, and any change to it. If a count is taking longer than usual, or your baby's movements have slowed, stopped or changed, Hold's answer is always the same: contact your midwife or maternity unit — don't wait to see if things settle.

The 5-1-1 guide it uses for contractions — about five minutes apart, about a minute long, kept up for about an hour — is standard patient-facing guidance, not a threshold Hold invented. Meeting it, or feeling worried before you do, both mean the same thing: call.

closing.heading: Built for the person who just wants to know
closing.body: No universal number, no diagnosis, no account required — just your baby's own pattern, timed in minutes on your own phone, and a plan for when labour starts.
